items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: And every New Years, we’re friends, his daughter, who now works for him in the office, I knew her when she was a little girl.

ctx.x: Oh, are we still rolling? Being at the right place at the right time is very important. And my career has always been that way. For most of us who were in the television/radio business, and many, many years ago I was the band leader at the Rainbow Room. The © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-

guy who ran it at that time was a restaurateur named Tony May, a really good restaurant. And somewhere along, he had a partner who in my mind was like Adolph Hitler, I mean he was like “Achtung,” everything had to be just so. And eventually they parted company and they lost the Rainbow Room, and then Tony May opened a very elegant Italian restaurant in New York City on Central Park South, a very posh area, San Domenico.
